statements: The deadline for sending the Commission's accounts to the Auditor General is set by section 21(2) of the Public Finance and Accountability (Scotland) Act 2000, which requires the account to be sent not later than 6 months after the end of the financial year to which it relates; the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 fixes no date, because paragraph 14 of schedule A1 leaves both preparation and sending to directions given by the Scottish Ministers.

Section 5(1)(a) of the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 requires the Commission, as soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, to submit to the Scottish Ministers and publish a report on the exercise of its functions during that year.
Section 5(4) of the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 requires the Scottish Ministers to lay before the Parliament a copy of each report submitted to them under section 5(1)(a).

Section 22(5) of the Public Finance and Accountability (Scotland) Act 2000 requires the Scottish Ministers to lay before the Parliament every account and report sent to them by the Auditor General and, except where the body has published them, to publish them, not later than 9 months after the end of the financial year.

The auditor's report on the account must set out the auditor's findings on the matters listed in section 22 of the Public Finance and Accountability (Scotland) Act 2000, including whether the expenditure and receipts shown were incurred or applied in accordance with the enactments and Budget Acts that authorised them.
